enonce_markdown: In bread mould (Mucor), the spores are produced inside the:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Identify the reproductive structure of the mould: it is the round head at the tip of an upright hypha.

### Solution

The upright hyphae (sporangiophores) bear sporangia at their tips, and the spores develop inside each sporangium. **Answer: a.**

enonce_markdown: A small outgrowth forms on a yeast cell, receives a copy of the nucleus and then separates from the parent cell. This type of asexual reproduction is called:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Name the process from the way the new individual forms.

### Solution

A new cell that grows out as a bud on the parent and then breaks off is formed by budding. Conjugation and fertilisation involve two cells joining, and fragmentation is the breaking up of a body into pieces. **Answer: c.**

enonce_markdown: A single sporangium of a mould releases a very large number of light spores. The main advantage of this is that:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Asexual spores are produced in large numbers because dispersal by air is a matter of chance.

### Solution

Spores are carried by air to unpredictable places. Producing very many of them increases the chance that some will land on suitable food with moisture and warmth. Spores are not gametes, and they do not fuse. **Answer: b.**

choix.texte: the offspring will be different from the parent
at least some spores will land on warm, moist food and grow
the spores can fuse to form a zygote
the spores are gametes that need a partner

enonce_markdown: Spores from the sporangium of a mould grow into new moulds. Compared with the parent mould, these new moulds are:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Asexual reproduction involves one parent and mitosis only.

### Solution

No gametes and no fertilisation are involved. The nuclei divide by mitosis, so each spore has the same genetic information as the parent and the offspring are identical to it. **Answer: d.**

choix.texte: genetically different, because two parents are involved
half as large, because they have half the chromosomes
a mixture of two parents, because of crossing over
genetically identical, because the spores are formed by mitosis from one parent

enonce_markdown: A spore of Rhizopus lands on a piece of moist bread. Describe the stages by which the spore develops into a new mould, and name the conditions the spore needs to grow.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Follow the life of one spore in order: landing, germination, growth of hyphae and formation of the mycelium.

### Solution

1. The spore lands on bread that is **moist and warm** and contains organic food.
2. It **germinates**: a hypha grows out of the spore.
3. The hypha grows and **branches** repeatedly. The hyphae digest the bread and absorb the food, and together they form a new **mycelium**.
4. After some time upright hyphae with sporangia grow from the mycelium and release new spores.

Conditions needed: **moisture, warmth and a supply of organic food** (a suitable substrate).

enonce_markdown:
A baker in Bafoussam leaves two identical slices of bread: one in a warm, humid cupboard and the other in a sealed, dry bag kept in a refrigerator. After four days only the first slice is covered by black mould.

(a) Explain these results.

(b) Suppose each of 5 sporangia on the mould releases 2 000 spores. Calculate the total number of spores released and explain why this large number is useful to the mould.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Reason from the conditions needed for germination, then from the role of numbers in dispersal by chance.

### Solution

(a) Spores are present in the air everywhere. They germinate only where there is **moisture, warmth and food**. The first slice is humid and warm, so the spores germinate and form a mycelium that produces black sporangia. The second is dry and cold and sealed, so spores cannot germinate and no mould grows.

(b) 5 x 2 000 = **10 000 spores**. Spores are dispersed by air and most fall on unsuitable places, so producing a very large number makes it likely that at least a few land on suitable food and grow.
